functions.name: InitializeComponentTables
functions.comment:
Initializes component data tables by loading Excel files for items, armor, and weapons

Algorithm:
1. Initialize ScreenshotConfig structure with field type definitions for Excel data parsing
2. Set up field type codes (4=string, 9=pointer) for version, alternategfx, spawnable, level, component, wclass, 2handedwclass, 1or2handed, and Transform fields
3. Call CreateExcelDataScreenshot three times to load Excel data:
   - Items data into pItemsData (stored at DAT_6f9a8c74)
   - Armor data into pArmorData (stored at DAT_6f9a8c7c)
   - Weapons data into pWeaponsData (stored at DAT_6f9a8c84)
4. Calculate total component count: DAT_6f9a8c68 = items + armor + weapons
5. Allocate combined buffer at source line 0xa29 (size = total * 0x1a8 bytes per component)
6. Store buffer base address in DAT_6f9a8c6c and DAT_6f9a8c70
7. Copy items data to combined buffer using REP MOVSD for dwords, REP MOVSB for remaining bytes
8. Advance buffer pointer by (items_count * 0x6a) and store in DAT_6f9a8c78
9. Copy armor data to buffer and advance pointer by (armor_count * 0x6a), store in DAT_6f9a8c80
10. Copy weapons data to buffer
11. Free temporary buffers for items, armor, and weapons data at lines 0xa39, 0xa3a, 0xa3b
12. Allocate lookup array at line 0xa40 (size = total * 2 bytes) and store in DAT_6f9a8c88
13. Zero-fill lookup array using REP STOSD and REP STOSB
14. Build component index by iterating through all components:
    - Check Transform field at offset +0xf6 for each component
    - If Transform field is 0, add component index to lookup array
15. Create string hashset at line 0xa4b and store handle in DAT_6f9a8ca0
16. Populate hashset by iterating through all components:
    - Add component name string at offset +0x80 to hashset using Ordinal_10215

Parameters:
  None (IMPLICIT: EDI register contains context pointer passed from caller)

Returns:
  void - Function updates global tables:
    - DAT_6f9a8c68: Total component count
    - DAT_6f9a8c6c/DAT_6f9a8c70: Combined component buffer base
    - DAT_6f9a8c78: Armor section start
    - DAT_6f9a8c80: Weapons section start
    - DAT_6f9a8c88: Component index lookup array
    - DAT_6f9a8ca0: Component name hashset

Special Cases:
  - Component structure size: 0x1a8 bytes (424 bytes)
  - Component name string offset: +0x80 (128 bytes from base)
  - Transform field offset: +0xf6 (246 bytes from base)
  - REP MOVSD optimization: copies 4 bytes at a time, remainder copied with REP MOVSB
  - Only components with Transform field = 0 are added to lookup array
  - 0x6a multiplier: 106 decimal, stride between sections after data copy

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type    | Description
-------|------|-----------------|---------|----------------------------------
+0x00  |  4   | version         | char*   | Component version string pointer
+0x80  |  4   | componentName   | char*   | Component name for hashset
+0xf6  |  2   | transformFlag   | short   | Transform flag (0=no transform)
Total size: 0x1a8 bytes (424 bytes) per component record

functions.name: RenderChatUserTooltip
functions.comment:
Renders a tooltip for Battle.net chat users showing user information.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pChatUser parameter (exit with error if NULL)
2. Initialize Unicode text buffer array (256 entries of Unicode strings)
3. Check if user flags match visible bitmask requirement
4. Calculate tooltip bounds rectangle around user position (-30 to +30 X, -80 to +20 Y)
5. Test if mouse point is within tooltip rectangle bounds
6. Initialize tooltip rendering context and invoke callbacks (7 iterations)
7. Check expansion type flag (0x44325850 = "D2XP") and add expansion line
8. Determine user role type and add corresponding role text line:
   - 0x13 = Moderator
   - 0x14 = Sysop  
   - 0x12 = Blizzard Rep
   - 0x17 = Speaker
   - 0x15 = Referee
   - 0x16 = VIP
   - 0x18 = Open Character
9. Check for string resource ID and add custom text if present
10. Decode product code and add product name line:
    - 0x44324456 (D2DV), 0x44325850 (D2XP), 0x44325354 (D2ST) = Diablo
    - 0x53534852 (SSHR) = Starcraft Shareware
    - 0x44545354 (DTST), 0x4452544c (DRTL) = Diablo
    - 0x44534852 (DSHR) = Diablo Shareware
    - 0x4a535452 (JSTR), 0x53544152 (STAR) = Starcraft
    - 0x53455850 (SEXP) = Brood War
    - 0x57335850 (W3XP) = Frozen Throne
    - 0x5732424e (W2BN) = Warcraft II
    - 0x57415233 (WAR3) = Warcraft III
11. Add "Realm: " line concatenated with realm name from offset 0x1ec
12. Add "Account Name: " line concatenated with account name from offset 0xcc
13. Calculate tooltip width bounds (clamp between 0 and 800 pixels)
14. Calculate tooltip height and adjust Y position for line count
15. Render tooltip background rectangle with border style 2
16. Validate line count does not exceed 7 (error and exit if exceeded)
17. Render each text line with appropriate color and centering
18. Return 1 for successful tooltip render

Parameters:
  pChatUser - Pointer to BattleNetChatUser structure containing user data

Returns:
  1 if tooltip was rendered successfully
  0 if user is NULL or point not in bounds

Special Cases:
  - NULL pointer triggers error message via Ordinal_10265(0x73d) and exit(-1)
  - Mouse must be within calculated rectangle bounds or returns 0
  - Line count exceeding 7 triggers error via Ordinal_10265(0x7f9) and exit(-1)
  - Product codes use 4-byte ASCII identifiers in big-endian format
  - Tooltip color value 3 used for Sysop and Blizzard Rep roles

BattleNetChatUser Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field            | Type        | Description
-------|------|------------------|-------------|---------------------------
0x00   | 4    | dwFlags          | DWORD       | User visibility flags
0x14   | 4    | dwPosX           | DWORD       | Screen X position
0x18   | 4    | dwPosY           | DWORD       | Screen Y position  
0x1c   | 4    | dwUserRole       | DWORD       | User role (0x12-0x18)
0xcc   | 170  | szAccountName    | wchar_t[85] | Unicode account name
0x1ec  | 170  | szRealmName      | wchar_t[85] | Unicode realm name
0x22c  | 4    | dwStringResource | DWORD       | String resource ID
0x230  | 4    | dwProductCode    | DWORD       | Game product ID

functions.name: RenderChatMessageUI
functions.comment:
Render chat message UI element with text formatting and color codes.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pChatMsg pointer is non-null (abort with error -1 if null)
2. Check visibility flag in dwFlags against global bitmask at gdwBitMasks_exref+0x4
3. Extract Y position from pChatMsg+0x18 and add base offset 6
4. Initialize 256-entry Unicode display buffer (512 bytes) to zeros
5. Extract message type from pChatMsg+0x1c and determine text color:
   - Type 0x14: Set color=3, useOutline=true
   - Type 0x12: Set color=3, useOutline=true
   - Otherwise if alternate flag set: color=1
6. Check if extended position flag set (bitmask+0x20) and add 15 to Y if true
7. Determine text source based on flags:
   - If system message flags (bitmask+0x18 or +0x1c) set:
     * Extract bit flags from dwFlags (bits 5-7, 12) to determine format parameters
     * Call Ordinal_10132 to format system message string
     * Convert Windows-1252 to Unicode via win2Unicode
     * Append expansion text from pChatMsg+0x14c
   - If expansion version detected (pChatMsg+0x230 == 'D2DV'/'D2ST'/'D2XP'):
     * Copy text directly from pChatMsg+0x14c (expansion text buffer)
   - Otherwise:
     * Copy text from pChatMsg+0xcc (classic text buffer)
8. Initialize temp buffer and check if additional text exists at pChatMsg+0x1cc
9. If additional text found:
   - Convert prefix string at 0x6f8fced8 to Unicode and append
   - Append text from pChatMsg+0x1cc
   - Convert suffix string at 0x6f8fced4 to Unicode and append
10. Call Ordinal_10184 for text preparation
11. Truncate Unicode string to 120 pixels width via TruncateUnicodeStringToPixelWidth
12. Calculate text pixel width and multi-line height
13. If useOutline flag set: Render text with black outline at (yPosition-1, 0) color 6
14. Render final text at (yPosition, 0) with determined color
15. Return 1 for success

Parameters:
IMPLICIT: pChatMsg passed in EBX register (custom Diablo II calling convention)
  pChatMsg - Pointer to chat message structure containing:
    +0x0: dwFlags - Message visibility and type flags
    +0x18: Base Y position coordinate
    +0x1c: Message type (0x12=whisper, 0x14=system, etc)
    +0xcc: Classic text buffer (204 bytes offset)
    +0x14c: Expansion text buffer (332 bytes offset)
    +0x1cc: Additional text buffer (460 bytes offset)
    +0x230: Version identifier (560 bytes: 'D2DV', 'D2ST', 'D2XP')

Returns:
  1 - Message rendered successfully
  0 - Message not visible (visibility flag check failed)

Special Cases:
- Null pointer triggers error code 0x6b0 via Ordinal_10265 and exits with code -1
- Message types 0x12 and 0x14 use color 3 (yellow) with black outline
- Version identifiers: 0x44324456='D2DV', 0x44325354='D2ST', 0x44325850='D2XP'
- Text truncated to 120 pixels (0x78) to fit UI constraints
- gdwBitMasks_exref contains global bitmask table for flag checking

functions.name: GetOrLoadScreenshotImage
functions.signature: int * GetOrLoadScreenshotImage(void * this, ScreenshotListNode * * ppScreenshotList, int classId, int cofComponent, void * pEntityId)
functions.comment:
Retrieves or loads a screenshot image for a game entity.

Algorithm:
1. Validate ppScreenshotList pointer is not NULL (error 0x4bf if NULL)
2. Search for existing screenshot node by entity ID using FindScreenshotNodeById
3. If node not found, initialize 257-byte COF file path buffer to zeros
4. Build COF file path using entity's class, component, and flags
5. If path build failed (empty buffer), return NULL
6. Allocate new ScreenshotListNode (8 bytes) via Ordinal_10042 (error 0x4ce if failed)
7. Initialize new node with NULL pointers for pScreenshotNode and pNext
8. Get or create screenshot cache node from file path (error 0x4d1 if failed)
9. Link cache node to list node and prepend to screenshot list
10. Return pImageData pointer from cache node at offset +0x14 (error 0x4d7 if NULL)

Parameters:
  ppScreenshotList - Pointer to head of screenshot linked list (ScreenshotListNode**)
  classId - Character class ID for COF file path
  cofComponent - COF component type (passed implicitly in EAX register)
  pEntityId - Entity identifier used for cache lookup

Returns:
  Pointer to image data (int*) from ScreenshotCacheNode.pImageData (+0x14)
  Returns NULL if COF file path build failed
  Calls _exit(-1) on allocation or cache errors

Special Cases:
  - Error 0x4bf: ppScreenshotList is NULL pointer
  - Error 0x4ce: Failed to allocate ScreenshotListNode
  - Error 0x4d1: Failed to create screenshot cache node
  - Error 0x4d7: Cache node created but pImageData is NULL
  - All errors trigger fatal exit via Ordinal_10265 + Ordinal_10024 + _exit(-1)

Structure Layout (ScreenshotCacheNode):
  Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type    | Description
  -------|------|---------------|---------|---------------------------
  +0x00  |  4   | refCount      | int     | Reference counter
  +0x04  |  4   | dwParam1      | DWORD   | Parameter 1
  +0x08  |  4   | dwParam2      | DWORD   | Parameter 2
  +0x0c  |  4   | dwParam3      | DWORD   | Parameter 3
  +0x10  |  4   | pFileHandle   | pointer | File handle pointer
  +0x14  |  4   | pImageData    | pointer | Image data pointer (returned)
  +0x18  |  4   | pPrev         | pointer | Previous cache node
  +0x1c  |  4   | pNext         | pointer | Next cache node
  Total: 32 bytes

Structure Layout (ScreenshotListNode):
  Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type    | Description
  -------|------|------------------|---------|---------------------------
  +0x00  |  4   | pScreenshotNode  | pointer | Points to ScreenshotCacheNode
  +0x04  |  4   | pNext            | pointer | Next list node
  Total: 8 bytes

functions.name: InitializeItemPropertyTables
functions.comment:
Initializes global item property lookup tables on first call.

Algorithm:
1. Check if already initialized via DAT_6f9aa67c flag, exit if true
2. Zero-initialize 0x2fd dwords at DAT_6f9a8cb0 (item property table)
3. Set initialization flag DAT_6f9aa67c = 1
4. Build property descriptor array with 23 entries (equiv1, equiv2, repair, shoots, quiver, throwable, reload, reequip, autostack, magic, normal, charm, beltable, costformula, varinvgfx, invgfx1-5)
5. Call Ordinal_10211 at 0xac0 to allocate screenshot data at DAT_6f9a8ca4
6. Call CreateExcelDataScreenshot with propertyConfig and 0xe4 parameter
7. Call Ordinal_10211 at 0xacc to allocate second data block at DAT_6f9a8c9c
8. Call CreateExcelDataScreenshot with second config and 0x4 parameter
9. Call InitializeComponentTables to set up component mapping tables
10. Initialize color lookup values from DAT_6f900c30
11. Set up three string constants: "lit " (0x2074696c), "med " (0x2064656d), "hvy " (0x20797668)
12. Iterate through all items in global item array at DAT_6f9a8c6c (count from DAT_6f9a8c68)
13. For each item: extract name pointer from offset +0x90 or +0x80 as fallback
14. Check item type compatibility using types 0x2d, 0x3, 0x33, 0x25, and 0x4b
15. Skip items matching certain type combinations (exclusion filter)
16. Search existing table entries to avoid duplicates
17. Find empty slot in table by checking type compatibility and empty entries
18. Store item name, type at +0x11e, and two color values from offsets +0xc0 and +0xc4
19. Increment entry count, advance to next item (stride 0x1a8 bytes)
20. Set terminator value DAT_6f9a98a4 = 0xff after processing all items

Parameters:
  None (implicit EDI register used as context pointer by callees)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  DAT_6f9aa67c - One-time initialization flag at 0x6f9aa67c
  DAT_6f9a8cb0 - Item property table base (0x2fd dwords = 3052 bytes)
  DAT_6f9a8c68 - Total item count
  DAT_6f9a8c6c - Item array base pointer
  Item stride: 0x1a8 bytes (424 bytes per item)
  Property IDs: 4, 6, 8, 9, 0xc, 0xe, 0x10-0x14, 0x16-0x19, 0x20, 0x23, 0x24, 0x44, 0x64, 0x84, 0xa4
  Type filters: 0x2d, 0x3, 0x33, 0x25, 0x4b (armor/weapon categories)
  Color lookup: DAT_6f900c6c entries, each 8 bytes (id at +0, value at +4)
  Max table entries: 255 (0xff terminator)

Structure Layout:
Item Entry (0x1a8 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type   | Description
-------|------|------------------|--------|----------------------------------
+0x80  |  4   | pFallbackName    | char*  | Fallback item name pointer
+0x90  |  4   | pPrimaryName     | char*  | Primary item name pointer  
+0xc0  |  4   | dwColorId1       | dword  | First color identifier
+0xc4  |  4   | dwColorId2       | dword  | Second color identifier
+0x11e |  2   | wItemType        | word   | Item type code

Property Table Entry (12 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type   | Description
-------|------|------------------|--------|----------------------------------
+0x0   |  4   | pItemName        | char*  | Item name pointer
+0x4   |  4   | dwItemType       | dword  | Item type from +0x11e
+0x8   |  4   | dwColorValue     | dword  | Color lookup result

functions.name: ValidateAndLoadScreenshot
functions.comment:
Validates screenshot context and loads screenshot image with fallback handling.

Algorithm:
1. Validate ESI context pointer is non-null, exit with error 0x80f if null
2. Check screenshot dimensions at ESI+0x1c/0x20/0x24 against max bounds (DAT_6f8ffdac/6f8ffe00/6f8ffe98)
3. Reset to default dimensions (7x5x1) if any dimension exceeds maximum allowed
4. Retrieve screenshot list pointer from ESI+0xb8
5. If screenshot list is null, report error 0x81c and exit
6. Attempt to load screenshot using custom dimensions from context
7. If load succeeds, return 1 (success)
8. On failure, reset to default dimensions (7x5x1) and retry with fallback
9. If fallback load succeeds, return 1 (success)
10. If both attempts fail, report error 0x82b and exit with -1

Parameters:
IMPLICIT ESI - Screenshot context pointer containing:
  +0x1c: dwWidth - Screenshot width dimension
  +0x20: dwHeight - Screenshot height dimension  
  +0x24: dwDepth - Screenshot depth/layer index
  +0xb8: ppScreenshotList - Pointer to screenshot list structure
IMPLICIT EDI - Additional context parameter passed to GetOrLoadScreenshotImage

Returns:
1 if screenshot loaded successfully
Function exits with -1 on critical errors (null context, null list, load failures)

Special Cases:
- Validates dimensions against global max values before loading
- Resets to safe defaults (7x5x1) if validation fails
- Provides two-stage fallback: custom dimensions first, then defaults
- Error codes: 0x80f (null context), 0x81c (null list), 0x82b (load failed)

functions.name: InitializeScreenshotRenderParams
functions.signature: void InitializeScreenshotRenderParams(int * pInputConfig, void * pScreenshotList, int * pOutputParams)
functions.comment:
Initialize screenshot rendering parameters from character configuration

Algorithm:
1. Copy width (offset +0x1c) and height (offset +0x20) from pInputConfig to pOutputParams +0xc and +0x10
2. Load character class index from pOutputParams +0x5 (byte)
3. Lookup and store three table values using indices from input:
   - Color table value at pOutputParams +0x1c (from DAT_6f8ffe08 using class index)
   - Unknown param at pOutputParams +0x28 (from DAT_6f8ffe5c using pInputConfig +0x24)
   - Another param at pOutputParams +0x18 (from DAT_6f8ffd48 using pInputConfig +0x1c)
4. Set default 'lit' value (0x2074696c = "til ") at pOutputParams +0x20
5. Check for custom lit value override in pInputConfig +0x38 array indexed by class
6. Validate screenshot list pointer at pInputConfig +0xb8, die with error 0x4f7 if null
7. Call GetOrLoadScreenshotImage to retrieve screenshot data pointer
8. Search through screenshot slot data (9-byte entries starting at +0x1c):
   - First byte = slot count, then array of [1 byte class + 8 bytes data]
   - Find entry matching character class index
   - Die with error 0x503 if class index >= 16
9. When match found:
   - Set pOutputParams +0x8 flag based on width > 6
   - Load value into pOutputParams +0x24 from DAT_6f8ffdb0 table using height index
   - Die with error 0x514 if lit value at pOutputParams +0x20 is zero
   - Call PadStringToFourBytes on slot data at offset +5
   - Clear pOutputParams +0x28 to zero
10. Validate three required parameters are non-zero:
    - pOutputParams +0x1c (error 0x520 if zero)
    - pOutputParams +0x18 (error 0x521 if zero)
    - pOutputParams +0x28 (error 0x522 if zero)
11. Set default values if still zero:
    - pOutputParams +0x20 = 0x20787878 ("xxx ") if zero
    - pOutputParams +0x24 = 0x20787878 ("xxx ") if zero

Parameters:
  pInputConfig - Pointer to input configuration structure with fields:
                 +0x1c = width (int)
                 +0x20 = height (int)
                 +0x24 = index for param lookup (int)
                 +0x38 = array of custom lit values indexed by class (int[])
                 +0xb8 = screenshot list pointer (void**)
  IMPLICIT in EAX
  
  pScreenshotList - Pointer to screenshot list node used for image loading
  IMPLICIT in EBX
  
  pOutputParams - Pointer to output structure to populate with fields:
                  +0x5 = character class index (byte)
                  +0x8 = width flag (1 if width > 6, else 0)
                  +0xc = width from input (int)
                  +0x10 = height from input (int)
                  +0x18 = param from table lookup (int)
                  +0x1c = color table value (int)
                  +0x20 = lit value (int, default 0x2074696c)
                  +0x24 = param from table lookup (int)
                  +0x28 = result from PadStringToFourBytes (int)
  IMPLICIT in ESI

Returns:
  void - Function terminates process via _exit(-1) on any validation failure

Special Cases:
  - 0x2074696c ("til ") = Default lit value
  - 0x20787878 ("xxx ") = Fallback value for +0x20 and +0x24 if still zero
  - Screenshot data format: [1 byte count][count * 9-byte entries]
  - Each 9-byte entry: [1 byte class][8 bytes data including 4-byte string at +5]
  - Maximum class index is 15 (dies with error 0x503 if >= 16)

Structure Layout:
Screenshot slot entry (9 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name        | Type  | Description
-------|------|-------------------|-------|----------------------------------
     0 |    1 | bClassIndex       | byte  | Character class identifier (0-15)
     1 |    4 | unknown1          | dword | Unknown field
     5 |    4 | szPaddedString    | char* | 4-byte padded string
Total: 9 bytes per slot entry

functions.name: InitializeUnitArmorData
functions.signature: void InitializeUnitArmorData(uint * pUnit, uint dwUnitType, uint pColorData, byte * pArmorColors, char * pConfigString)
functions.comment:
Initializes unit armor and equipment configuration data.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input unit pointer is not NULL, allocate 0x85b bytes for armor data
2. Initialize allocated data to zero and store pointer at unit offset +0xb8
3. Create unit back-reference at offset +0x1c
4. Determine item category: if unit type < 7, call GetItemTypeCategoryFromBodyLocations
5. Store item category at offset +0x24, exit if category is zero
6. Store unit type parameter at offset +0x20
7. Load and apply bit masks from global gdwBitMasks_exref (3 masks at offsets 0, 4, 8)
8. Loop 16 times (armor slots):
   - Initialize slot flag field (offset +0x40) to 1
   - If color byte is 0 or 0xff, clear slot (value = 0)
   - Otherwise call ValidateAndCycleArmorType, load color from DAT_6f9a8cb0 table
   - Load type flags from DAT_6f9a8cb8 table at offset +0x40
9. Process 4 groups of 4 color bytes (16 bytes total) with sentinel handling:
   - Decrement each byte if not 0xff sentinel value
   - Otherwise leave as-is
10. Validate and load screenshot data via ValidateAndLoadScreenshot
11. If screenshot valid, call Ordinal_10093 for finalization

Parameters:
pUnit - Pointer to unit/player structure to initialize
dwUnitType - Unit type identifier (compared against threshold of 7)
pColorData - Pointer to armor color lookup table
pArmorColors - Pointer to 16 color byte values (4 groups of 4)
pConfigString - Configuration string pointer

Returns:
void - Function modifies unit structure in-place

Special Cases:
- 0xff is sentinel value for color bytes, not decremented
- Unit types < 7 use special item category lookup
- Allocation failure causes exit(-1) with error logging
- Early return if item category validation fails
- Structure size 0x85b (2139 bytes) allocated for armor data

functions.name: AllocateAndInitializeUnit
functions.signature: UnitAny * AllocateAndInitializeUnit(byte * armorTypeArray, char * colorPaletteArray, uint unitType, uint unknown2)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a new unit entity structure.

This function allocates memory for a new unit/entity, initializes its fields with
default values, sets armor types and color palettes, and validates the unit before
linking it into the active unit list. The function validates armor indices and color
values, ensuring they are within valid ranges before storing them in the unit structure.
If validation fails, it returns NULL and cleans up the allocated memory.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate main unit structure (0xc65 bytes)
2. If allocation fails, log error and exit with code -1
3. Zero-initialize the entire unit structure (141 dwords)
4. Allocate color data buffer (0x85b bytes)
5. If allocation fails, log error and exit with code -1
6. Initialize color data to zero
7. Store color data pointer at unit offset +0xb8
8. Initialize item property tables
9. Store unit type (0-6) at unit offset +0x1c
10. Calculate armor category from unit type at unit offset +0x24
11. Apply global bit masks to unit flags (offsets +0x00, +0x04, +0x08)
12. Loop through 16 armor slots, validating and storing armor types
13. Loop through 4 color palette entries (16 bytes), decrementing non-0xff values
14. Validate armor and color data using ValidateAndLoadScreenshot
15. Call Ordinal_10093 for additional validation
16. Link unit into active unit list by updating list pointers
17. Return pointer to initialized unit, or NULL if validation fails

Parameters:
  armorTypeArray : byte * - Array of 16 armor type indices (0-255), 0 or 0xff = empty
  colorPaletteArray : char * - Array of 16 color palette values to apply to unit
  unitType : uint - Unit type identifier (0-6 = specific types, 7+ = default type)
  unknown2 : uint - Implicit parameter (loaded from stack at different offset)

Returns:
  UnitAny * - Pointer to newly allocated and initialized unit structure
              NULL if armor allocation fails, color allocation fails, or validation fails

Special Cases:
  - Armor types 0x00 and 0xff mark empty/invalid armor slots
  - Color values 0xff are preserved as-is, all others are decremented by 1
  - Unit types 0-6 have category lookups, type 7+ always gets category 1
  - If ValidateAndLoadScreenshot fails, function returns NULL
  - If Ordinal_10093 validation fails, function returns NULL

functions.name: SetupScreenshotRenderParams
functions.signature: void SetupScreenshotRenderParams(ScreenshotRenderParams * pParams, void * pInputConfig, byte bClassIndex)
functions.comment:
Initialize screenshot render parameters with character and configuration data

Algorithm:
1. Store configuration value from EAX register to pParams +0x34 (dwConfigValue field)
2. Store character class index byte parameter to pParams +0x5 (bCharClass field)
3. Store source parameter from ECX register to pParams +0x40 (dwSourceParam field)
4. Store texture/image ID from EDX register to pParams +0x0 (dwTextureId field)
5. Call InitializeScreenshotRenderParams to populate remaining fields:
   - Passes ESI (screenshot list pointer) as first implicit parameter
   - Passes return address as second implicit parameter
   - Passes pParams as third explicit parameter
6. Set bit 0x2 in flags field at pParams +0x44 using OR operation

Parameters:
  pParams - Pointer to ScreenshotRenderParams structure to initialize (passed on stack +0x8)

  pInputConfig - Pointer to input configuration structure (passed on stack +0xc)

  bClassIndex - Character class index byte to store at +0x5 (passed on stack +0x10)

  eax_configValue - Configuration or state value to store at +0x34
  IMPLICIT in EAX

  ecx_sourceParam - Source parameter value to store at +0x40
  IMPLICIT in ECX

  edx_textureId - Texture/image identifier to store at +0x0
  IMPLICIT in EDX

  esi_screenshotList - Screenshot list pointer passed to InitializeScreenshotRenderParams
  IMPLICIT in ESI

Returns:
  void - Initializes pParams structure with screenshot rendering parameters

Special Cases:
  - 0x2 = Flag bit set at +0x44 indicating parameter initialization complete
  - Function uses custom calling convention with EAX, ECX, EDX, and ESI registers
  - Relies on InitializeScreenshotRenderParams to populate most structure fields
  - ESI and return address are passed implicitly to called function
  - Returns with RET 0xc instruction, caller cleans 12 bytes from stack

Structure Layout:
ScreenshotRenderParams (at least 72 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type  | Description
-------|------|-----------------|-------|----------------------------------
   0x0 |    4 | dwTextureId     | uint  | Texture/image identifier from EDX
   0x5 |    1 | bCharClass      | byte  | Character class index (0-15)
   0x8 |    4 | bWidthFlag      | uint  | Width comparison flag (set by called func)
   0xc |    4 | nWidth          | int   | Screenshot width (set by called func)
  0x10 |    4 | nHeight         | int   | Screenshot height (set by called func)
  0x18 |    4 | dwParam1        | uint  | Table lookup parameter
  0x1c |    4 | dwColorValue    | uint  | Color table value
  0x20 |    4 | dwLitValue      | uint  | Lighting value (default 0x2074696c)
  0x24 |    4 | dwParam2        | uint  | Table lookup parameter
  0x28 |    4 | dwPaddedString  | uint  | 4-byte padded string result
  0x34 |    4 | dwConfigValue   | uint  | Configuration/state value from EAX
  0x40 |    4 | dwSourceParam   | uint  | Source parameter from ECX
  0x44 |    4 | dwFlags         | uint  | Status flags (bit 0x2 set here)
Total: 72 bytes minimum

functions.name: RenderAnimatedUIControl
functions.comment:
RenderAnimatedUIControl - Renders an animated UI control with screenshot frames and text overlays

Algorithm:
1. Validate control pointer in EBX register (implicit parameter), exit with error 0x5e8 if null
2. Check control flags at offset +0x0 against global bitmask table to determine if control should be rendered
3. If special flag (gdwBitMasks_exref+0x28) is set, render top text overlay at position (X+5, Y-5)
4. If text pointer at offset +0xbc is non-zero, render bottom text at position (X-20, Y-60) with color from +0xc0
5. Validate render enabled flag at offset +0xb8, exit with error 0x617 if disabled
6. Look up screenshot node by ID (offset +0x20) in screenshot list (offset +0x24)
7. Validate screenshot data pointer at node+0x14, exit with error 0x620 if null
8. Validate screenshot type at offset +0x4 and current frame at offset +0x8 against bounds
9. Determine render mode based on control flags: mode 1 if flags 0x14 and 0x10 set, or flag 0x34 set; otherwise mode 5
10. Loop through all animation frames (count from screenshot data):
    - Validate frame index through bitfield table
    - Get chat UI node from packed index array at offset +0x28 if index != 0xff
    - Call Ordinal_10041 render function with frame data and chat node
11. Update animation frame counter at offset +0x8 by adding frame increment from offset +0x10
12. Reset frame counter to 0 if it exceeds max frames at offset +0xc
13. Update global animation tick timers (DAT_6f9a9e38, DAT_6f9a9e44, DAT_6f9a9e50) every 66ms (0x42 ticks)
14. If debug flag (gdwBitMasks_exref+0x24) is set, render debug counter text at position (X, Y+10)
15. Return TRUE (1) on success

Parameters:
  dwRenderFlags - Rendering flags passed to Ordinal_10041 (stack parameter)
  IMPLICIT EBX - Pointer to UIAnimatedControl structure (custom calling convention)

Returns:
  BOOL - TRUE (1) if rendering succeeded, FALSE (0) if control is null or flags disabled

Special Cases:
  - Error 0x5e8: Control pointer is NULL
  - Error 0x5f3: Global animation system disabled (DAT_6f9a9e48 == 0)
  - Error 0x617: Render enabled flag is 0
  - Error 0x620: Screenshot data pointer is NULL
  - Error 0x625: Screenshot bounds validation failed
  - Error 0x666: Debug value is NULL when debug flag set
  - Animation timer threshold: 0x42 (66 decimal) milliseconds
  - Chat index sentinel: 0xff indicates no chat UI node

UIAnimatedControl Structure Layout (164 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name              | Type  | Description
-------|------|-------------------------|-------|------------------------------------------
  +0x0 |   4  | dwFlags                 | DWORD | Control flags checked against bitmask table
  +0x4 |   1  | bType                   | BYTE  | Screenshot/control type identifier
  +0x5 |   1  | bScreenshotType         | BYTE  | Screenshot subtype for bounds validation
  +0x6 |   2  | wPadding                | WORD  | Alignment padding
  +0x8 |   4  | dwCurrentFrame          | DWORD | Current animation frame (fixed-point 8.8)
  +0xc |   4  | dwMaxFrames             | DWORD | Maximum frame count before reset
 +0x10 |   4  | dwFrameIncrement        | DWORD | Frame advance rate per tick
 +0x14 |   4  | dwPosX                  | DWORD | Screen X coordinate
 +0x18 |   4  | dwPosY                  | DWORD | Screen Y coordinate
 +0x20 |   4  | dwScreenshotId          | DWORD | Screenshot resource identifier
 +0x24 |   4  | pScreenshotList         | PTR   | Pointer to ScreenshotListNode array
 +0x28 | 118  | abChatPackedIndices[118]| ARRAY | Chat UI node indices per frame (0xff = none)
 +0xb8 |   4  | dwRenderEnabled         | DWORD | Enable flag for rendering
 +0xbc |   4  | dwTextPointer           | DWORD | Pointer to text string for overlay
 +0xc0 |   1  | bTextColor              | BYTE  | Text color index
 +0xc1 |   1  | bTextStyle              | BYTE  | Text style/font flags
-------|------|-------------------------|-------|------------------------------------------
Total: 164 bytes (offsets up to +0xc1)

functions.name: CalculateScreenshotMemoryRequirements
functions.signature: int CalculateScreenshotMemoryRequirements(byte * pClassIndexArray, int nArrayOffset, int * pTotalSize, byte bCharClass, int nAnimFrame)
functions.comment:
Calculate total memory required for rendering screenshots of multiple character classes

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pConfigContext (EBX) is not null, abort with error 0x57c if null
2. Check if class index array has any entries (*pClassIndexArray == 0), return 0 if empty
3. Loop through each character class index in the array up to *pClassIndexArray count
4. For each class index at offset (nArrayOffset + i):
   - Validate class index is less than 0x10 (16 classes), abort with error 0x583 if invalid
   - Zero-initialize 0x48 bytes (72 bytes) of ScreenshotRenderParams structure on stack
   - Set renderParams.dwCharClassExtended = bCharClass (extended to UINT)
   - Set renderParams.dwUnknownParam = 0
   - Set renderParams.dwTextureId = nAnimFrame
   - Set renderParams.bCharClass = current class index from array
   - Call InitializeScreenshotRenderParams(pOutputParams_edi, pScreenshotList, pLoopIndex)
   - Set renderParams.dwRenderFlags |= 2 (enable specific render flag)
   - Call Ordinal_10005(&renderParams, 0, 1) to process screenshot rendering
   - If Ordinal_10005 succeeded and returned non-zero handle:
     * Call Ordinal_10069(handle) to get size of this screenshot
     * Add size to pConfigContext->dwBaseOffset (+0x14)
     * Compare against *pTotalSize, update *pTotalSize if larger
     * Increment nProcessedCount
5. Return nProcessedCount (number of successfully processed character classes)

Parameters:
  pClassIndexArray - Pointer to array where first byte is count, remaining bytes are class indices
  nArrayOffset - Offset into class index array to start reading indices
  pTotalSize - Pointer to DWORD that receives maximum cumulative size requirement
  bCharClass - Character class identifier passed to render params
  nAnimFrame - Animation frame number for screenshot rendering
  pConfigContext (EBX) - IMPLICIT: Pointer to configuration context with dwBaseOffset at +0x14
  pScreenshotList (ESI) - IMPLICIT: Pointer to screenshot list data structure
  pOutputParams_edi (EDI) - IMPLICIT: Pointer to output parameters structure

Returns:
  Number of character class screenshots successfully processed (0 to *pClassIndexArray)
  Returns 0 if array is empty or all renders failed
  Never returns on error (calls _exit(-1) for invalid inputs)

Special Cases:
  - Error 0x57c: pConfigContext (EBX) is null - fatal error
  - Error 0x583: Class index >= 0x10 (16) - invalid class index, fatal error
  - Size accumulates using max(*pTotalSize, current + base_offset) pattern
  - Uses stdcall convention: callee cleans 0x14 (20) bytes from stack (5 parameters)

Structure Layout - ScreenshotRenderParams (renderParams, 72 bytes):
  Offset | Size | Field Name           | Type | Description
  -------|------|----------------------|------|------------------------------------------
  +0x00  |  4   | dwTextureId          | UINT | Set to nAnimFrame parameter
  +0x04  |  4   | field_0x4            | UINT | Initialized to 0
  +0x05  |  1   | bCharClass           | BYTE | Set to current class index from array
  +0x06  |  2   | field_0x6            | WORD | Initialized to 0
  +0x0B  |  4   | bWidthFlag           | UINT | Initialized to 0
  +0x34  |  4   | dwUnknownParam       | UINT | Set to 0
  +0x40  |  4   | dwCharClassExtended  | UINT | Extended byte value of bCharClass param
  +0x44  |  4   | dwRenderFlags        | UINT | OR'd with 2 before Ordinal_10005 call
  (Total: 72 bytes, only relevant fields documented)

functions.name: RenderAnimatedControlScreenshots
functions.comment:
Render screenshot images for animated UI control based on class indices.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pControl pointer is not null (error 0x5a8 if null)
2. Check control flags at +0x0 against global bit masks at gdwBitMasks_exref and +0x8
3. Return early if either required flag bit is not set
4. Load adjusted X position (pControl+0x14 - 2) and Y position (pControl+0x18)
5. Verify screenshot enabled flag at pControl+0xb8 is non-zero (error 0x5b8 if disabled)
6. Call FindScreenshotNodeById with pControl+0x24 (dwScreenshotId) and pControl+0x20 (pScreenshotList)
7. Validate screenshot node has valid pScreenshotNode+0x14 pointer (error 0x5c0 if null)
8. Call ValidateScreenshotPointer to verify screenshot data integrity
9. Extract frame index from pControl+0x8 (dwCurrentFrame >> 8)
10. Extract screenshot type from pControl+0x4 (bScreenshotType)
11. Call ValidateScreenshotBoundsOrDie with screenshot type and frame index
12. Obtain class index array and count via nClassCount return value (error 0x5c5 if zero)
13. Call CalculateScreenshotMemoryRequirements to validate rendering feasibility
14. Return early if memory calculation returns <= 0 or first class count is zero
15. Loop through class indices in array, exit when bCurrentClassIndex >= 0x10 (error 0x5cf)
16. For each valid class index: zero initialize 0x48-byte renderParams structure with REP STOSD
17. Call SetupScreenshotRenderParams to populate render parameters with class-specific data
18. Call Ordinal_10011 to render screenshot at adjusted position (nAdjustedPosX, dwPosY)
19. Increment class iterator and continue until all classes processed
20. Return normally after all screenshots rendered successfully

Parameters:
pControl - Pointer to UIAnimatedControl structure containing animation state and screenshot configuration
IMPLICIT EDI - Context pointer used by FindScreenshotNodeById (passed implicitly via register)

Returns:
void - No return value, exits process on fatal validation errors

Special Cases:
- Error 0x5a8: pControl is null pointer
- Error 0x5b8: Screenshot rendering disabled (pControl+0xb8 == 0)
- Error 0x5c0: Screenshot node has null data pointer
- Error 0x5c5: No class indices returned from validation
- Error 0x5cf: Invalid class index >= 0x10 (max 16 classes supported)
- All errors call Ordinal_10265 for error formatting, Ordinal_10024 for logging, and exit(-1)
- Function returns early (no error) if control flags don't match required masks
- Function returns early (no error) if memory calculation fails or class count is zero
- Adjusted X position is control's dwPosX - 2 (likely accounts for border or padding)

Structure Layout - UIAnimatedControl (partial):
Offset  Size  Field Name           Type      Description
------  ----  -------------------  --------  ---------------------------
+0x00   4     dwFlags              dword     Control state and type flags
+0x04   1     bScreenshotType      byte      Screenshot variant identifier
+0x08   4     dwCurrentFrame       dword     Current animation frame (high byte = index)
+0x14   4     dwPosX               dword     Screen X coordinate
+0x18   4     dwPosY               dword     Screen Y coordinate
+0x20   4     pScreenshotList      pointer   Screenshot linked list head
+0x24   4     dwScreenshotId       dword     Screenshot identifier for lookup
+0xb8   4     dwRenderEnabled      dword     Screenshot rendering enable flag

functions.name: SetObjectFieldValue
functions.comment: Setting prototype: uint SetObjectFieldValue(int * pObjectPtr, int fieldValue)

functions.name: RenderScreenshotRegion
functions.comment:
Renders a screenshot region to the display buffer with alpha blending.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that texture type is 10 (screenshot texture)
2. Exit with error if validation fails (writes error to log)
3. Check if render flags match required bitmasks at gdwBitMasks_exref+0 and +8
4. Return 0 if bitmask validation fails
5. Call Ordinal_10049 to get alpha value from color table at 0x6f922338
6. Load dimensions and offsets from render parameters structure
7. Calculate scaled Y offset by multiplying field at +0x14 by float at +0x40
8. Convert floating point offset to integer using rounding
9. Call Ordinal_10014 to render the rectangular region with alpha blending
10. Return 1 on successful render

Parameters:
  pRenderParams - ScreenshotRenderParams* - Pointer to screenshot rendering parameters
    IMPLICIT: Parameter passed in ECX register (__fastcall convention)

Returns:
  1 if screenshot region was successfully rendered
  0 if bitmask validation failed
  Does not return if texture type validation fails (calls _exit)

Special Cases:
  - Texture type must be 10 or function exits process with code -1
  - Both bitmask checks at gdwBitMasks_exref must pass for rendering
  - Alpha value retrieved from global color table at 0x6f922338
  - Uses render mode 5 (alpha blending mode)
  - Y offset calculation uses floating point scaling factor

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type  | Description
-------|------|-----------------|-------|----------------------------------

functions.name: AllocateGameObjectNode
functions.signature: undefined4 * AllocateGameObjectNode(uint dwGameType, uint dwGameSubtype, uint param1, uint param2, uint dwFlags, void * pOptionalCoordinates)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a new game object node with parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Push registers (EBX, EBP, ESI, EDI) for function prologue
2. Initialize ESI to 0 for loop counter
3. Load memory allocator address and allocation size (0x44 bytes)
4. Call memory allocation routine at 0x6f8e7678
5. Store allocated pointer in EDX and EDI
6. Zero-initialize 0x11 (17) dwords of memory using STOSD
7. Set first dword to 0xa (sentinel value)
8. Load global flags from 0x6f8fb17c
9. OR global flags with allocated structure at offset +0x8
10. Load additional global flags at offset +0x8 and apply mask
11. Set field at offset +0x14 to stack parameter at [ESP+0x14]
12. Initialize multiple structure fields with parameters (offsets +0x4, +0xc, +0x10, +0x18, +0x1c, +0x24-+0x34, +0x3c, +0x40)
13. Check if global list head at 0x6f9014a0 is NULL
14. If NULL, store allocated node as new list head
15. If not NULL, traverse linked list following +0x3c pointers to find tail
16. Link new node to tail's +0x3c field
17. Return pointer to allocated structure in EAX
18. Clean stack with RET 0x8

Parameters:
  dwGameType - uint - Game object type identifier (ECX register)
  dwGameSubtype - uint - Game object subtype (EDX register)
  param1 - uint - Additional parameter 1 (Stack[0x4])
  param2 - uint - Additional parameter 2 (Stack[0x8])
  dwFlags - uint - Flags and configuration bits (Stack[0xc])
  pOptionalCoordinates - void * - Optional coordinate data pointer (Stack[0x10])

Returns:
  undefined4 * - Pointer to newly allocated game object node structure

Special Cases:
  Empty list condition: If gpGameObjectListHead is NULL, new node becomes the head
  Non-empty list: Traverses to tail node and appends new node
  Sentinel value: First dword initialized to 0xa before other fields
  Linked list field: Offset +0x3c used for next node pointer navigation

Structure Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name        | Type    | Description
  -------|------|-------------------|---------|------------------------------------
  +0x00  |  4   | sentinel_value    | dword   | Initialized to 0xa
  +0x04  |  4   | field_type        | dword   | Type field
  +0x08  |  4   | flags_combined    | dword   | Combined global and parameter flags
  +0x0c  |  4   | param1_value      | dword   | Parameter 1 from ECX
  +0x10  |  4   | param2_value      | dword   | Parameter 2 from EDX
  +0x14  |  4   | stack_param       | dword   | Stack parameter at +0x14
  +0x18  |  4   | field_24          | dword   | Additional parameter field
  +0x1c  |  4   | callback_ptr      | dword   | Callback function pointer
  +0x24  |  4   | field_36_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  +0x28  |  4   | field_40_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  +0x2c  |  4   | field_44_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  +0x30  |  4   | field_48_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  +0x34  |  4   | field_52_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  +0x3c  |  4   | pNext             | dword   | Linked list next pointer
  +0x40  |  4   | field_64_zeros    | dword   | Initialized to 0
  -------|------|-------------------|---------|------------------------------------
  Total: 68 bytes

functions.name: RemoveUIControlFromListThunk
functions.comment:
Thunk/jump stub that forwards to RemoveUIControlFromList (0x6f8f7fc0)

This is an ordinal export (Ordinal_10092) that simply redirects execution to the actual implementation.

functions.name: CopyInitializationData
functions.comment:
Copies initialization data from a static data table to a destination buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Load source pointer to DAT_6f932a38 (3136-dword initialization data table)
2. Set up copy counter to 0xc40 (3136) dwords
3. Loop: Copy dword from source to destination, increment both pointers, decrement counter
4. Return after all dwords copied

Parameters:
pDestBuffer: Pointer to destination buffer where initialization data will be copied (passed in ECX per __fastcall)

Returns:
void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Copies exactly 3136 dwords (12544 bytes total)
- Initialized as part of program startup or module initialization
- Source data is static and located at 0x6f932a38

functions.name: FindNearestColorIndex
functions.signature: byte FindNearestColorIndex(byte red, byte green, byte blue)
functions.comment:
Finds the nearest palette index for a given RGB color triplet.

This function is a wrapper around FindNearestPaletteColor that searches the global color palette to find the palette index of the color closest to the input RGB triplet. Used by text rendering functions to convert arbitrary RGB colors to valid palette indices.

Algorithm:
1. Load red component from [ESP + 0xc] via MOVZX EAX
2. Load green component from [ESP + 0x8] via MOVZX ECX
3. Load blue component from [ESP + 0x4] via MOVZX EDX
4. Push blue component (EDX) to stack
5. Push green component (ECX) to stack
6. Push red component (EAX) to stack
7. Push flag value 0x100 (color matching mode)
8. Push palette pointer 0x6f922338 (global color palette)
9. Call FindNearestPaletteColor to search for best match
10. Return palette index in EAX
11. Caller cleans stack with RET 0xc

Parameters:
  red - Red component value (0-255)
  green - Green component value (0-255)
  blue - Blue component value (0-255)

Returns:
  Byte representing the palette index (0-255) of the nearest matching color

Special Cases:
  Global palette is at 0x6f922338
  Flag value 0x100 indicates standard color matching mode
  Used by text rendering control functions

functions.name: SetGameEventTimerState
functions.comment:
Initializes or toggles the game event timer system.

When enabled (bEnable != 0): activates the timer by setting the event_enabled flag, capturing the current tick count, initializing state, and invoking the event processor.
When disabled (bEnable == 0): deactivates the timer by clearing the event_enabled flag and invoking the event processor for cleanup.

Parameters:
  bEnable: Timer activation flag (non-zero enables, zero disables)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  Magic value 0x2 at offset 0x6f921630 indicates specific event processor state
  Global 0x6f922338 is the event data structure passed to event processor
  GetTickCount() provides wall-clock milliseconds for timer initialization

functions.name: UpdateGameTimerAndTriggerCallback
functions.comment:
Updates game timer and triggers periodic callback if elapsed time threshold is met.

Algorithm:
1. Check if initialization flag (DAT_6f8ffd44) is set; return if not set
2. If active condition flag (DAT_6f9a9e28) is set:
   a. Call GetTickCount() to get current system tick count
   b. Calculate elapsed time as current ticks minus last update timestamp (DAT_6f9a9e2c)
   c. Compare elapsed time to 0x7d0 (2000 milliseconds)
   d. If elapsed time less than 2000ms, return early (threshold not met)
   e. Update last timestamp by calling GetTickCount() again and storing in DAT_6f9a9e2c
   f. Decrement timer counter (DAT_6f921630) by 1
   g. If counter is still positive (>0), proceed to trigger callback
   h. If counter reached 0 or below, clear active condition flag (DAT_6f9a9e28)
3. Clear initialization flag (DAT_6f8ffd44) to 0
4. Call UpdateGameTimerAndTriggerCallback() with address of callback data structure (DAT_6f922338)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Threshold value 0x7d0 = 2000 milliseconds, indicating 2-second update interval
- Counter-based timing: allows multiple timer cycles before complete shutdown
- Early return paths avoid unnecessary processing if conditions not met
- Flags control enable/disable state of timer mechanism

Global Variables Used:
- DAT_6f8ffd44: Initialization/enable flag (0=disabled, non-zero=enabled)
- DAT_6f9a9e28: Active condition flag (0=inactive, non-zero=active)
- DAT_6f9a9e2c: Last GetTickCount() timestamp for interval measurement
- DAT_6f921630: Countdown counter for timer cycles
- DAT_6f922338: Callback data structure address passed to UpdateGameTimerAndTriggerCallback

functions.name: GetDataTableEntry
functions.comment:
Returns pointer to indexed entry in data table.

Algorithm:
1. Shift index left by 8 bits (multiply by 256) to convert array index to 64-byte offset (256 >> 2 = 64)
2. Add base address of data table (0x6f9c5994)
3. Return computed pointer

Parameters:
- nIndex (int): Zero-based array index

Returns:
- void *: Pointer to the indexed entry in the data table. Each entry is 64 bytes apart.

Magic Numbers:
- 0x8: Left shift amount (multiply index by 256, which equals 64 * 4 for 32-bit pointer arithmetic)
- 0x40 (64): Entry stride in bytes

functions.name: InitializePointerArraysAndCallOrdinal10022
functions.comment:
Initialize pointer arrays and invoke Ordinal_10022

Algorithm:
1. Initialize three static data pointers (0x6f93db60, 0x6f94db60, 0x6f95db60)
2. Build first array of 49 pointers starting at 0x6f932a38 with 0x100-byte stride
   - Each entry points to a 256-byte (0x100) memory region
   - Array spans from 0x6f932a38 to 0x6f935b38
3. Build second array of 13 pointers starting at 0x6f921638 with 0x100-byte stride
   - Each entry points to a 256-byte (0x100) memory region
   - Array spans from 0x6f921638 to 0x6f922338
4. Initialize seven static region pointers (0x6f901630, 0x6f911630, 0x6f922738, 
   0x6f932838, 0x6f935b38, 0x6f932738, 0x6f932938)
5. Pass pointer to stack structure containing all initialized data to Ordinal_10022

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - Function performs initialization only

Special Cases:
- First array stride: 0x100 bytes (256 bytes per region)
- Second array stride: 0x100 bytes (256 bytes per region)
- First array count: 49 entries (calculated from (0x6f935b38 - 0x6f932a38) / 0x100)
- Second array count: 13 entries (calculated from (0x6f922338 - 0x6f921638) / 0x100)
- Stack frame size: 0x120 bytes (288 bytes)

Structure Layout:
Stack frame organization passed to Ordinal_10022:
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type        Description
------  ----  ----------------------  ----------  ---------------------------
+0x00   4     pFirstDataPointer       void*       First data region pointer
+0x04   4     pSecondDataPointer      void*       Second data region pointer
+0x08   4     pThirdDataPointer       void*       Third data region pointer
+0x0C   196   arrayPointers1[49]      void*[]     Array of 49 region pointers
+0xD0   52    arrayPointers2[13]      void*[]     Array of 13 region pointers
+0x104  4     pStaticRegion1          void*       Static region pointer 1
+0x108  4     pStaticRegion2          void*       Static region pointer 2
+0x10C  4     pStaticRegion3          void*       Static region pointer 3
+0x110  4     pStaticRegion4          void*       Static region pointer 4
+0x114  4     pStaticRegion5          void*       Static region pointer 5
+0x118  4     pStaticRegion6          void*       Static region pointer 6
+0x11C  4     pStaticRegion7          void*       Static region pointer 7
Total: 288 bytes (0x120)

functions.name: LoadPaletteAndInitializeColorTables
functions.comment:
Loads palette file and initializes color lookup tables for rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Call CreateAndSaveScreenshotFile to get RGB palette data pointer
2. Build 256-entry RGBA color table with alpha=0 from RGB triplets
3. Open palette file using Ordinal_10102, exit with error if open fails
4. Validate file handle is non-zero, exit with error 0x59 if null
5. Read palette data from file using Ordinal_10105
6. On read failure, copy local buffer and exit with error 0x5f
7. Allocate 0xcf-sized buffer using Ordinal_10042 for palette data
8. Call ValidateScreenshotParameters to verify palette buffer integrity
9. Exit with error 0x49 if validation fails
10. Close file handle using Ordinal_10103
11. Copy palette buffer to 11 global arrays at different offsets:
    - DAT_6f922338 (0x400 bytes, offset +0x0)
    - DAT_6f93db60 (0x30000 bytes, offset +0xd40)
    - DAT_6f932a38 (0x3100 bytes, offset +0x100)
    - DAT_6f911630 (0x10000 bytes, offset +0x10d40)
    - DAT_6f901630 (0x10000 bytes, offset +0xcd40)
    - DAT_6f934a38 (0x1000 bytes, offset +0x900)
    - DAT_6f935a38 (0x100 bytes, offset +0xd00)
    - DAT_6f935b60 (0x8000 bytes, offset +0x14d40)
    - DAT_6f922738 (0x10000 bytes, offset +0x16d40)
    - DAT_6f932838 (0x100 bytes, offset +0x1ad40)
    - DAT_6f935b38 (0x27 bytes, offset +0x1ad80)
    - DAT_6f921638 (0xd00 bytes, offset +0x6b627)
12. Set alpha channel to 5 for all 256 palette entries
13. Generate two color index tables by scaling RGB values:
    - Scale to 170% brightness (0xaa/100) clamped to 0xff
    - Store in DAT_6f932738 using Ordinal_10049
    - Create red-only table in DAT_6f932938 (R channel, GB=0)
14. Call InitializePointerArraysAndCallOrdinal10022 to set up data structures
15. Call Ordinal_10061 with base palette pointer
16. Call Ordinal_10043 twice with codes 0x96 and 0x99
17. Return 1 for success

Parameters:
- palettePath: Path to palette data file (.dat or .pl2 format)

Returns:
- 1 on success
- Exits process with -1 on file errors

Special Cases:
- Error 0x59: File open failure
- Error 0x5f: File read failure
- Error 0x49: Palette validation failure
- RGB values scaled by 170/255 for brightness adjustment
- All RGB components clamped to 0xff maximum

functions.name: InitializePaletteAndColorTables
functions.comment:
Initializes game color palettes and color lookup tables.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nPaletteMode is 0 (use default Act 1 palette)
2. If mode 0: Format default palette file paths using sprintf
   - Build path for palette ACT file (palette_act1.pal.dat)
   - Build path for palette PL2 file (palette_act1.pal.pl2)
3. Load the palette file using LoadPaletteAndInitializeColorTables
4. Initialize all color lookup tables using InitializeColorTables
5. Return 1 on success

Parameters:
- nPaletteMode: Palette selection mode (0=default Act 1, non-zero=custom)
- pszPalettePath: Path to custom palette file when nPaletteMode != 0

Returns:
- 1: Always returns success (palette initialization completed)

Special Cases:
- Mode 0 uses hardcoded Act 1 palette files from DATA_GLOBAL directory
- Custom palette path ignored when nPaletteMode is 0
- Both InitializeColorTables calls occur regardless of mode selection

Structure Layout:
- Local stack buffers: 260 bytes each for palette file paths
- Total local stack space: 520 bytes (0x208)

functions.name: InitializePaletteAndGraphics
functions.comment:
Initializes palette and graphics subsystem for the specified palette index.

Algorithm:
1. Extract palette index from lower 8 bits of input parameter and add 1
2. Validate palette index range [1-5]; clamp to 1 if out of bounds
3. Format primary palette file path using index (DATA/GLOBAL.xx, palette index, pal_dat)
4. Format secondary palette file path using index (DATA/GLOBAL.xx, palette index, pal_pl2)
5. Load palette from secondary path and initialize color tables
6. Copy graphics buffer to target and invoke graphics vtable at offset 0x70
7. Return palette initialization result

Parameters:
paletteIndex: Input palette index (0-255 range, lower 8 bits extracted)

Returns:
uint: Result of palette initialization (0=success, non-zero=error code)

Special Cases:
- Palette index automatically clamped to range [1-5]
- Out-of-range indices default to palette 1
- Function constructs file paths dynamically using sprintf
- Palette files: pal_dat (primary data), pal_pl2 (secondary data)

functions.name: DispatchEventHandler
functions.comment:
Dispatches event callbacks for registered event handlers with validation and recursion tracking.

Algorithm:
1. Load handler pointer from EventContext and validate handler type is 6 (screenshot/UI event)
2. If type invalid, log error message at ordinal 0x259 and exit process with code -1
3. Validate event is not system event (0x102) and handler's registered event type matches context
4. If validation passes and primary callback exists, mark handler as active (offset +0x4c = 1)
5. Check global recursion depth counter (DAT_6f9014a8) is positive
6. If recursion depth invalid, log error at ordinal 0x263 and exit process
7. Invoke primary callback function (offset +0x24) passing EventContext pointer
8. If post-callback exists (offset +0x28), increment recursion counter and invoke with stack context
9. Decrement recursion counter after post-callback completes
10. Return callback result or 0 if validation failed

Parameters:
  pEventContext (EventContext*) - Pointer to event context containing handler reference and event metadata

Returns:
  uint - Primary callback return value, or 0 if validation failed or no callback invoked

Special Cases:
  - Handler type must be exactly 6, otherwise process terminates with error 0x259
  - Event type 0x102 (system event) is rejected
  - Recursion depth must be positive (DAT_6f9014a8 > 0) or process exits with error 0x263
  - Post-callback receives modified stack context at ESP+0xc containing original handler pointer

Structure Layout - EventContext (12 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type    Description
------  ----  ------------  ------  -----------
0x00    4     pHandler      ptr     Pointer to event handler structure
0x04    4     field_0x04    uint    Event flags (rejected if 0x102)
0x08    4     eventType     uint    Event type identifier

Structure Layout - Event Handler (accessed fields, 84+ bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type    Description
------  ----  ------------  ------  -----------
0x00    4     dwType        uint    Handler type (must be 6)
0x24    4     fpCallback    ptr     Primary callback function pointer
0x28    4     fpPostCb      ptr     Post-callback function pointer (optional)
0x4c    4     bActive       uint    Active status flag (set to 1 when dispatching)
0x50    4     dwEventType   uint    Registered event type to match

functions.name: ProcessEventHandlerCallback
functions.comment:
Processes an event handler by validating its type, checking bitmask flags, and invoking registered callbacks if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference pointer to get handler structure
2. Validate handler type equals 6, exit with error 0x232 if invalid
3. Set handler flags at +0x8 by ORing with gdwBitMasks[1]
4. Check if handler flags match required bitmask conditions (gdwBitMasks[2] and gdwBitMasks[0])
5. If flags invalid, clear gdwInvBitMasks[1] bits and return 0
6. Check if handler state at +0x40 has bits 0-1 clear (not in progress)
7. Clear field at +0x44 to mark handler as ready
8. If callback pending at +0x48 exists and function pointer at +0x34 valid, validate global counter DAT_6f9014a8 > 0
9. If counter invalid, exit with error 0x243
10. Invoke callback function pointer with ppEventHandler parameter
11. Clear pending callback flag at +0x48
12. Clear gdwInvBitMasks[1] bits from handler flags and return callback result

Parameters:
ppEventHandler (void **) - Pointer to event handler pointer, dereferenced to access handler structure

Returns:
uint - Callback function return value on success, 0 if conditions not met or handler skipped

Special Cases:
- Type value 6 expected at offset +0x0, program exits with -1 if mismatch (error 0x232)
- DAT_6f9014a8 must be > 0 to invoke callbacks, exits with -1 if not (error 0x243)
- Bits 0-1 at offset +0x40 control handler processing state (must be clear)
- Global bitmask arrays control flag manipulation: gdwBitMasks (set), gdwInvBitMasks (clear)

Structure Layout (Handler):
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type          | Description
-------|------|---------------|---------------|----------------------------------
+0x0   | 4    | dwType        | uint          | Handler type, must be 6
+0x8   | 4    | dwFlags       | uint          | Handler state flags
+0x34  | 4    | fpCallback    | function ptr  | Callback function pointer
+0x40  | 1    | bState        | byte          | Processing state flags (bits 0-1)
+0x44  | 4    | dwReadyFlag   | uint          | Ready state indicator (cleared)
+0x48  | 4    | dwPendingFlag | uint          | Pending callback flag (cleared after call)

functions.name: ProcessUnitAnimation
functions.comment:
Process animation state changes for unit objects

Algorithm:
1. Dereference ppUnit parameter to obtain actual UnitAny pointer
2. Validate unit type equals 6 (UNIT_OBJECT)
3. Check required bit masks against unit flags at gdwBitMasks_exref+8 and gdwBitMasks_exref
4. If toggle flag (bit 1) at offset +0x40 is set, invert current frame values
5. If toggle flag not set and frames are non-zero, return success immediately
6. If toggle flag not set and frames are zero, initialize both to 1
7. If ordinal flag (bit 2) not set, call Ordinal_10070 for additional processing
8. If event handler flags (bits 0-1) are clear, return success
9. Load event handler function pointer from offset +0x34
10. Verify event handler is not NULL
11. Check global animation enable flag DAT_6f9014a8
12. If global flag disabled, trigger fatal error with code 0x221
13. Call event handler function pointer with ppUnit parameter
14. Return success (1)

Parameters:
ppUnit - Pointer to UnitAny pointer (double indirection for object reference)

Returns:
1 - Animation processing succeeded
0 - Validation failed (invalid type or missing required flags)

Special Cases:
- Unit type must be exactly 6 (UNIT_OBJECT), otherwise fatal error 0x1fd
- Both bit masks at gdwBitMasks_exref and gdwBitMasks_exref+8 must be set
- Toggle flag inverts frame counter states (0->1, non-zero->0)
- Function terminates process on invalid type or disabled global animation
- Event handler may be NULL (skipped if so)

Structure Layout (UnitAny offsets):
Offset | Size | Field         | Type    | Description
-------|------|---------------|---------|----------------------------------
+0x00  |  4   | dwType        | DWORD   | Unit type (must be 6 for objects)
+0x08  |  4   | dwFlags       | DWORD   | Unit flags validated against masks
+0x34  |  4   | pEventHandler | pointer | Animation event callback function
+0x40  |  4   | _pad40        | DWORD   | Animation control flags (bits 0-2)
+0x44  |  4   | dwCurrentFrame| DWORD   | Current animation frame counter
+0x48  |  4   | _pad48        | DWORD   | Secondary frame counter or state

functions.name: CheckPointInBounds
functions.comment:
Checks if a point (x, y) is within the bounds of a rectangle.

Algorithm:
1. Load left boundary from pBounds->x at offset +0xc
2. Check if nX >= left boundary, jump to return_false if less
3. Load bottom boundary from pBounds->y at offset +0x10
4. Calculate height by subtracting top offset at +0x18 from bottom
5. Check if nY >= calculated height, jump to return_false if less
6. Load width from pBounds->width at offset +0x14
7. Calculate right boundary by adding width to left (x + width)
8. Check if nX < right boundary, jump to return_false if greater or equal
9. Check if nY < bottom boundary, jump to return_false if greater or equal
10. Return true (1) if all bounds checks pass

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT: pBounds - Pointer to BoundsRect structure (passed in EAX)
            +0xc: x (left boundary)
            +0x10: y (bottom boundary)
            +0x14: width (horizontal extent)
            +0x18: offset (top boundary for height calculation)
  IMPLICIT: nX - X coordinate to test (passed in ESI)
  IMPLICIT: nY - Y coordinate to test (passed in EDI)

Returns:
  true (1) - Point is within rectangle bounds
  false (0) - Point is outside rectangle bounds

Special Cases:
  - Uses inclusive lower bounds (>=) and exclusive upper bounds (<)
  - Height calculated as (bottom - top) where top is at offset +0x18
  - All comparisons are signed integer comparisons
  - Custom calling convention: EAX=pBounds, ESI=nX, EDI=nY

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type   | Description
-------|------|------------|--------|----------------------------------
  +0xc |    4 | x          | int    | Left boundary of rectangle
 +0x10 |    4 | y          | int    | Bottom boundary of rectangle
 +0x14 |    4 | width      | int    | Width of rectangle
 +0x18 |    4 | offset     | int    | Top offset for height calculation
Total size: 16 bytes (BoundsRect structure)

functions.name: ValidateAndStoreScreenshotConfig
functions.comment:
Validates screenshot configuration type and stores screenshot index in config object.

Algorithm:
1. Verify that pConfigObject type field equals 6 (validates config is screenshot type)
2. If validation fails, dispatch error handler and terminate process
3. Store screenshotIndex at offset 0x9c (156 bytes) in pConfigObject
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
- pConfigObject (ECX): Pointer to configuration object with type validation at offset 0
- screenshotIndex (EDX): Screenshot index to store at offset 0x9c

Returns:
void - Does not return on validation failure (calls _exit), otherwise returns normally

Special Cases:
- Validation checks for exact type value of 6
- If type != 6, function never returns (calls _exit with -1)
- Screenshot index stored at fixed offset 0x9c (156 bytes from base)
- Error message includes screenshot format string "oScreenshot%03d.jpg"

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0      | 4    | dwType     | int  | Configuration type (must be 6)
156    | 4    | nIndex     | int  | Screenshot index storage

functions.name: ProcessKeyEventHandler
functions.comment:
Processes keyboard event handler and invokes callback if conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Validate event handler type equals 6 (keyboard event type)
2. If validation fails, log error with Ordinal_10265 and exit(-1)
3. Check event handler flags against global bitmask at gdwBitMasks_exref
4. Verify both required bitmask conditions are set (offset +0x0 and +0x8)
5. Ensure state fields dwState1 and dwState2 are both zero
6. Check key direction matches handler direction flags:
   - If nKeyDirection > 0, verify bFlags has bit 0x8 set (key down)
   - If nKeyDirection < 0, verify bFlags has bit 0x10 set (key up)
7. Verify fpCallback is non-null at offset +0x34
8. If all conditions pass, increment global handler counter at 0x6f9014a8
9. Initialize 32-byte event context structure on stack with zeroed fields
10. Store pEventHandler pointer in context at offset 0x0
11. Invoke fpCallback with pointer to context structure
12. Decrement global handler counter
13. Return 0 (success)

Parameters:
  pEventHandler (KeyEventHandler* in EAX) - Pointer to keyboard event handler structure
  nKeyDirection (int in ESI) - Key direction: positive for key down, negative for key up
  IMPLICIT: Uses EAX for pEventHandler parameter (non-standard calling convention)
  IMPLICIT: Uses ESI for nKeyDirection parameter (non-standard calling convention)

Returns:
  0 - Success, event processed
  Does not return if validation fails (calls exit(-1))

Special Cases:
  - Handler type must equal 6 or function terminates process
  - Both dwState1 (+0x44) and dwState2 (+0x48) must be zero
  - Key direction determines which flag bit is checked (0x8 for down, 0x10 for up)
  - Global counter at 0x6f9014a8 tracks active handler execution depth

Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description
-------|------|---------------|-------|------------------------------------------
  0x00 |   4  | dwType        | uint  | Event type, must equal 6 for keyboard
  0x08 |   4  | dwFlags       | uint  | Event flags checked against bitmasks
  0x34 |   4  | fpCallback    | dword | Function pointer to event callback
  0x40 |   1  | bFlags        | byte  | Direction flags: 0x8=down, 0x10=up

  0x48 |   4  | dwState2      | uint  | State field 2, must be zero
Total structure size: 76 bytes

functions.name: ValidateAndSetStructureField
functions.comment:
Validates object type and assigns value to field at offset +0x5c.

This function validates that the provided structure is of type 6, then writes

void - No return value

functions.name: ProcessGameObjectCallback
functions.comment:
Processes game object callbacks and timed events.

Validates the game object type, then dispatches primary and secondary callback functions with proper state management. Increments/decrements a global activity counter around secondary callback execution.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference the input node to get the game object structure
2. Validate that the object type field (offset +0x0) equals 6
3. If invalid type, call error handler and exit with code -1
4. Check for primary callback function pointer at offset +0x24
5. If primary callback exists:
   - Set activity flag at offset +0x4C to 1
   - Call primary callback with object node as parameter
6. Check for secondary callback function pointer at offset +0x28
7. If secondary callback exists:
   - Increment global activity counter (0x6f9014a8)
   - Call secondary callback with stack frame reference
   - Decrement global activity counter
8. Return

Parameters:
  pObjectNode (ECX): Pointer to GameObjectNode wrapper containing game object reference
    - pObjectNode[0] contains the actual game object structure
    - Game object type must equal 6

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Magic number 6 is the expected game object type identifier
  - Global counter 0x6f9014a8 tracks active secondary callbacks
  - Offset 0x4C flag indicates primary callback execution state
  - Error code 0xBC (188) is logged on type validation failure

functions.name: SetObjectProperties
functions.signature: void SetObjectProperties(void * pObject, int property0, int property1, int property2, int property3)
functions.comment:
Sets four integer property values on a game object structure.

2. If validation fails:

- property0: First property value to store at offset +0xc
- property1: Second property value to store at offset +0x10
- property2: Third property value to store at offset +0x14
- property3: Fourth property value to store at offset +0x18

Returns:
void - No return value

- Invalid type triggers process exit with code -1
- RET 0xc indicates callee cleanup of 12 bytes (4 parameters)

functions.name: InitializeSecondaryConfig
functions.signature: void InitializeSecondaryConfig(void * pConfigObject, int dwDataValue, int nConfigParam, int param4)

Initialize secondary configuration object with validation.

- Error code 0x96 (150 decimal) indicates type validation failure
- GetSecondaryText() provides dynamic text that is Unicode-aware

functions.name: InitializeScreenshotSlotWithValidation
functions.signature: void InitializeScreenshotSlotWithValidation(int * pScreenshotSlot, int nScreenshotIndex, Unicode * pFilename, int nConfigMode)
functions.comment:

nScreenshotIndex (int): Screenshot slot index to store at offset +0x60

functions.name: ValidateAndSetEntityMode
functions.comment:
Validates entity type field and sets mode-related fields

functions.name: DestroyAnimatedUIControl
functions.comment:
Destroys an animated UI control (type 6) by validating type and removing from control list.

This function implements cleanup for type 6 animated UI controls as part of the UI
control destruction dispatcher (DestroyUIControl). It validates that the control type
is exactly 6, then delegates to RemoveUIControlFromList for resource cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that control type (stored at pControl[0]) equals 6
2. If type is not 6, call DispatchDynamicFunction for potential recovery

4. Exit with code -1 on type validation failure

0      | 4    | dwType     | dword  | Control type (must be 6 for animated controls)

functions.name: RenderCellFileText
functions.comment:
Renders text from a CellFile context structure with optional secondary text line

Algorithm:
1. Call Ordinal_10184 to initialize rendering state
2. Retrieve text height from global font data table indexed by DAT_6f8ffd34
3. Get primary Unicode text string from context offset +0x64 (100 bytes into structure)
4. Calculate primary text width using Unicode::strlen and Ordinal_10055
5. Calculate primary Y position: (context.y - (context.height - textHeight)/2) + yOffset
6. Check if frame pointers exist at offsets +0x44, +0x48, or +0x4c and add 2 pixel offset if present
7. Check bit 0x40 of flags at offset +0x40 to determine if dual-text rendering is enabled
8. If dual-text mode enabled:
   a. Retrieve secondary text using Ordinal_10003
   b. Calculate secondary text dimensions
   c. Calculate positions using height/3 division instead of height/2
   d. Apply frame offsets if borders exist
   e. Render secondary text at calculated position using RenderFormattedUnicodeText
9. Render primary text at final calculated position using RenderFormattedUnicodeText

Parameters:
  this (ESI): Pointer to CellFile rendering context structure
  yOffset: Vertical offset adjustment for text positioning

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Negative Y positions are clamped to 0
  - Text centering uses integer division by 2 for single text, by 3 for dual text
  - Frame offset of 2 pixels applied when borders present
  - Dual-text flag 0x40 enables secondary text line with thirds-based positioning
  - Text width constraint from context offset +0x264
  - Color/style parameter from context offset +0x270

Structure Layout (CellFile Context):
  Offset | Size | Field Name      | Type   | Description
  -------|------|-----------------|--------|----------------------------------
  +0x0C  |  4   | xPos            | int    | Base X coordinate
  +0x10  |  4   | yPos            | int    | Base Y coordinate  
  +0x14  |  4   | width           | int    | Context width for centering
  +0x18  |  4   | height          | int    | Context height for centering
  +0x40  |  1   | flags           | byte   | Bit 0x40 = dual-text mode
  +0x44  |  4   | pFrameBorder1   | ptr    | First frame border pointer
  +0x48  |  4   | pFrameBorder2   | ptr    | Second frame border pointer
  +0x4C  |  4   | pFrameBorder3   | ptr    | Third frame border pointer
  +0x60  |  4   | contextData     | dword  | Additional context data
  +0x64  | var  | unicodeText     | wchar* | Primary Unicode text string
  +0x264 |  4   | maxTextWidth    | int    | Maximum text width constraint
  +0x270 |  2   | textColor       | word   | Text color or style parameter

functions.name: RenderCellFileContext
functions.comment:
Renders a cell file context to the screen with block-based processing.

Algorithm:
1. Validate cell context type equals 6, exit with error -1 if invalid
2. Load bit masks from gdwBitMasks_exref and check rendering flags at +0x8
3. Calculate render offset based on animation state and offset values
4. If callback data exists at +0x4 and bit mask 8 is set, perform block rendering
5. Divide dimensions into 256-byte blocks for width (+0x14) and height (+0x18)
6. Loop through height blocks, calling Ordinal_10041 for each 256x256 tile
7. Process final partial row if height not evenly divisible by 256
8. Determine quality level based on size: 4 if >35, 3 if ==32, 2 if >20, else 1
9. Store quality at +0x60, initialize field +0x264 to 0
10. If animation enabled (+0x64 != 0), call FUN_6f8ef8d0 with quality parameter
11. Update animation frame counter at +0x4c: reset to 0 if ==2, else increment
12. If callback function exists at +0x268, check visibility and invoke callback
13. Return 1 to indicate successful rendering

Parameters:
  pCellContext - Pointer to cell file context structure (628 bytes minimum)
                 +0x0: dwType (must equal 6)
                 +0x4: pCallbackData
                 +0x8: dwRenderFlags
                 +0xc: nSourceX
                 +0x10: nDestWidth
                 +0x14: nSourceWidth
                 +0x18: nDestHeight
                 +0x40: bFlags
                 +0x44: pAnimationData
                 +0x48: nAnimationFrame
                 +0x4c: nAnimationState
                 +0x54: dwBlockOffset1
                 +0x58: dwBlockOffset2
                 +0x5c: nCurrentOffset
                 +0x60: nQualityLevel
                 +0x64: wAnimationEnabled
                 +0x264: dwResetValue
                 +0x268: pCallbackFunction
                 +0x26c: bIsVisible

Returns:
  1 - Rendering completed successfully

Special Cases:
  - Type validation: Calls Ordinal_10265(0x14d) and exits with -1 if type != 6
  - Block size: Processes in 256-byte (0x100) blocks for tiled rendering
  - Quality levels: 1-4 based on size thresholds at 20, 32, and 35 pixels
  - Blend modes: 1 for flags &0x20, 5 for standard masked rendering
  - Visibility check: Uses global clip rectangle at 0x6f901488/0x6f90148c
  - Callback nesting: Increments DAT_6f9014a8 before callback, decrements after
